name: Viscous Fingering
desc: A Hele-Shaw cell in close-up: air forced into viscous oil between two glass plates cannot hold a smooth front, so the interface buckles into Saffman-Taylor fingers that stretch, widen and tip-split forever while surface tension fights to keep them fat — injected as glowing dye in dark oil, false-color pressure interferogram, bitten sumi litho plate, electroplated metal dendrite, or ironbow thermal flux.

energy.doc: drive pressure and exposure — injection speed, tip glow, fringe count and contrast (the master knob)

scale.doc: magnification onto the injection point — guaranteed visible change

speed.doc: growth rate and inject/withdraw cycle rate (0.2 still creeps)

density.doc: finger COUNT — inverse surface tension: 0 = a few fat lobes, 1 = the front shatters into fine dendritic fingers

aniso.doc: crystalline anisotropy — 0 = isotropic Saffman-Taylor lobes, 1 = six-fold snowflake dendrites on a slowly creeping axis

hue.doc: hue of the injected phase (the oil takes the complement)

x.doc: injection point across the plate (also centers the magnified view)

style.doc: aesthetic: lab plate of glowing dye in dark oil / false-color pressure fringes / bitten sumi litho / electroplated metal dendrite under raking light / ironbow thermal flux

seed.doc: deterministic seed for the nucleus perturbation and plate grain
